coral_triangle.name: Coral Triangle
coral_triangle.remarks: Around six hundred species of reef-building coral live here, which is roughly three quarters of every kind there is. Everything about diving in this part of the world follows from that.

south_china_sea.name: South China Sea
south_china_sea.remarks: Shallow, warm, heavily fished and claimed by almost everyone with a coast on it.

philippine_sea.name: Philippine Sea
philippine_sea.remarks: Contains the Mariana Trench, and with it the deepest water on the planet — nearly eleven kilometres, which is further down than most aircraft fly up.

sulu_sea.name: Sulu Sea
sulu_sea.remarks: Deep water with isolated atolls rising out of it, the best known being a reef park two hours from anywhere by boat.

celebes_sea.name: Celebes Sea
celebes_sea.remarks: A deep basin between three island groups, with walls dropping from the surface to well past two thousand metres.

banda_sea.name: Banda Sea
banda_sea.remarks: Deep, current-swept and volcanic. Hammerheads pass through in season, and the islands beneath were once the only source of nutmeg in the world.

molucca_sea.name: Molucca Sea
molucca_sea.remarks: Where three tectonic plates meet, which accounts for both the volcanoes and the abrupt depths.

java_sea.name: Java Sea
java_sea.remarks: Shallow throughout — mostly under fifty metres — because it is drowned land rather than proper ocean floor.

flores_sea.name: Flores Sea
flores_sea.remarks: Volcanic islands, strong tidal flow between them, and manta rays making use of it.

andaman_sea.name: Andaman Sea
andaman_sea.remarks: Limestone pinnacles rising out of deep water, with visibility that swings wildly depending on which monsoon is in charge.

bay_of_bengal.name: Bay of Bengal
bay_of_bengal.remarks: The largest bay in the world, and fed by enough river silt to make the water the colour of tea for a long way offshore.

gulf_of_thailand.name: Gulf of Thailand
gulf_of_thailand.remarks: Shallow and warm, averaging under sixty metres. Where a great many people do their first open water course.

strait_of_malacca.name: Strait of Malacca
strait_of_malacca.remarks: One of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, and shallow enough that the largest ships have to think about it.

persian_gulf.name: Persian Gulf
persian_gulf.remarks: Shallow, hot and very salty — summer water temperatures over thirty-five degrees, which is warmer than most people find comfortable in a wetsuit or out of one.

gulf_of_oman.name: Gulf of Oman
gulf_of_oman.remarks: The way in and out of the Persian Gulf, with seasonal upwelling that brings cold green water and whale sharks with it.

east_china_sea.name: East China Sea
east_china_sea.remarks: Shallow continental shelf with the Kuroshio Current running along its edge, dragging warm water and tropical species much further north than they have any business being.

sea_of_japan.name: Sea of Japan
sea_of_japan.remarks: Nearly enclosed, and cold enough at depth that the water below three hundred metres is a uniform one degree.

yellow_sea.name: Yellow Sea
yellow_sea.remarks: Named for the silt the rivers dump into it, which is also a fair description of the visibility.

sea_of_okhotsk.name: Sea of Okhotsk
sea_of_okhotsk.remarks: Freezes over in winter, which is unusual at this latitude and down to the cold air arriving off Siberia.

timor_sea.name: Timor Sea
timor_sea.remarks: Shallow shelf with a deep trough along its northern edge, and tides that run over ten metres on the Australian side.

arafura_sea.name: Arafura Sea
arafura_sea.remarks: Shallow enough that it was dry land during the last ice age, when Australia and New Guinea were joined.

laccadive_sea.name: Laccadive Sea
laccadive_sea.remarks: Warm water between India, the Maldives and Sri Lanka, and the corridor blue whales use through the region.

afghanistan.name: Afghanistan
afghanistan.remarks: Landlocked and mountainous, and about as far from a reef as it is possible to get in Asia.

armenia.name: Armenia
armenia.remarks: Landlocked, with Lake Sevan sitting at nearly two thousand metres — high enough that diving it is an altitude problem.

azerbaijan.name: Azerbaijan
azerbaijan.remarks: On the Caspian, which is the largest lake on Earth and called a sea largely out of habit.

bahrain.name: Bahrain
bahrain.remarks: An island state in shallow Gulf water, with a pearl-diving history that ran for four thousand years before oil arrived.

bangladesh.name: Bangladesh
bangladesh.remarks: Built almost entirely out of river delta, and the Sundarbans mangrove forest along its coast is the largest anywhere.

bhutan.name: Bhutan
bhutan.remarks: Landlocked and Himalayan, with rivers that start under glaciers.

brunei.name: Brunei
brunei.remarks: A small stretch of Borneo coast with a surprising number of wrecks offshore, several of them from the Second World War.

cambodia.name: Cambodia
cambodia.remarks: Islands off the southern coast with reef around them, and a lake inland that quadruples in size every monsoon.

china.name: China
china.remarks: Fourteen thousand kilometres of coast across three seas, and a tropical island at the southern end where the diving actually happens.

georgia.name: Georgia
georgia.remarks: Black Sea coast with mountains immediately behind it, and caves in the limestone that go a very long way down.

india.name: India
india.remarks: Seven thousand kilometres of coast, atolls off the south-west, and a monsoon that decides for six months of the year whether anyone is diving at all.

indonesia.name: Indonesia
indonesia.remarks: Seventeen thousand islands sitting on the join between three tectonic plates, in the middle of the Coral Triangle. More marine species than anywhere, and current on most of them.

iran.name: Iran
iran.remarks: Coast on the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, with islands offshore and mountains a long way behind.

iraq.name: Iraq
iraq.remarks: Under sixty kilometres of coast at the head of the Gulf, where two great rivers arrive together.

israel.name: Israel
israel.remarks: A dozen kilometres of Red Sea coast at Eilat, with reef a short swim from the beach, and a Mediterranean coast at the other end of the country.

japan.name: Japan
japan.remarks: Nearly seven thousand islands along a subduction zone, with warm current running up the Pacific side and cold water on the other. Diving ranges from coral in the far south to ice in Hokkaido.

jordan.name: Jordan
jordan.remarks: Twenty-seven kilometres of Red Sea coast, and all of it reef. Also the Dead Sea, where the salinity is such that diving is essentially impossible.

kazakhstan.name: Kazakhstan
kazakhstan.remarks: The largest landlocked country in the world, with a Caspian shore and what is left of the Aral Sea.

kuwait.name: Kuwait
kuwait.remarks: Shallow Gulf water that reaches bath temperature in summer and cools enough in winter to need a wetsuit.

kyrgyzstan.name: Kyrgyzstan
kyrgyzstan.remarks: Landlocked and mountainous, with Issyk-Kul — a lake at sixteen hundred metres that never freezes, despite the winters.

laos.name: Laos
laos.remarks: The only landlocked country in South-East Asia, and dependent on the Mekong for very nearly everything.

lebanon.name: Lebanon
lebanon.remarks: Two hundred kilometres of Mediterranean coast, with Phoenician harbours under parts of it.

malaysia.name: Malaysia
malaysia.remarks: Split across two land masses. Sipadan, off the Borneo side, is an old volcanic cone rising six hundred metres from the seabed, and the turtles there are essentially furniture.

maldives.name: Maldives
maldives.remarks: Twenty-six atolls, and the lowest country on Earth — the highest natural point is under two and a half metres. The tide runs hard through the channels, which is where the mantas feed.

mongolia.name: Mongolia
mongolia.remarks: Landlocked between two large neighbours, and further from any ocean than almost anywhere else on the planet.

myanmar.name: Myanmar
myanmar.remarks: The Mergui Archipelago runs down its southern coast — eight hundred islands, most uninhabited, and only opened to divers relatively recently.

nepal.name: Nepal
nepal.remarks: Landlocked, and containing the highest point on the planet — which is made of marine limestone, laid down on a seabed before India arrived.

north_korea.name: North Korea
north_korea.remarks: Coast on two seas, and effectively closed to visiting divers.

oman.name: Oman
oman.remarks: Seasonal upwelling turns the water cold and green and brings whale sharks in with it. The Daymaniyat Islands are a reserve, and turtles nest along the whole coast.

pakistan.name: Pakistan
pakistan.remarks: A thousand kilometres of Arabian Sea coast, with mangroves at the Indus delta and rock further west.

palestine.name: Palestine
palestine.remarks: A short Mediterranean coastline at Gaza, and no practical diving access to it.

philippines.name: Philippines
philippines.remarks: Seven and a half thousand islands inside the Coral Triangle. Thresher sharks off Malapascua, a reef park in the middle of the Sulu Sea, and macro life that people fly a long way to photograph.

qatar.name: Qatar
qatar.remarks: A peninsula into shallow Gulf water, with pearl banks offshore that supported the country before oil.

saudi_arabia.name: Saudi Arabia
saudi_arabia.remarks: Eighteen hundred kilometres of Red Sea coast, much of it barely dived, and reef systems that are only now being properly surveyed.

singapore.name: Singapore
singapore.remarks: One of the busiest ports anywhere, and a country that has grown measurably larger by reclaiming its own seabed.

south_korea.name: South Korea
south_korea.remarks: Cold water and strong tides, and the haenyeo of Jeju — women who have free-dived for shellfish for centuries and mostly still do.

sri_lanka.name: Sri Lanka
sri_lanka.remarks: Blue whales year-round off the southern coast, which is unusual — most populations migrate, and this one largely does not.

syria.name: Syria
syria.remarks: A short Mediterranean coast with several thousand years of harbours along it.

taiwan.name: Taiwan
taiwan.remarks: Sits where the warm Kuroshio Current runs north, which brings coral and tropical fish a long way up the latitude scale.

tajikistan.name: Tajikistan
tajikistan.remarks: Landlocked and over ninety percent mountain, with glacial lakes at altitudes that make any diving a serious calculation.

thailand.name: Thailand
thailand.remarks: Two coasts with opposite monsoons, so something is always in season. The Similans on the Andaman side are granite boulders underwater rather than reef, which surprises people.

timor_leste.name: Timor-Leste
timor_leste.remarks: Deep water arrives within metres of the beach along the north coast, so most of the diving is done by walking in.

turkmenistan.name: Turkmenistan
turkmenistan.remarks: Landlocked apart from the Caspian, and about eighty percent desert.

united_arab_emirates.name: United Arab Emirates
united_arab_emirates.remarks: Coast on both sides of the peninsula — hot shallow Gulf water on one, cooler and clearer Gulf of Oman on the other.

uzbekistan.name: Uzbekistan
uzbekistan.remarks: One of only two doubly landlocked countries on Earth, and the site of the Aral Sea's disappearance.

vietnam.name: Vietnam
vietnam.remarks: Three thousand kilometres of coast, with reef around the southern islands and limestone karst rising out of the water in the north.

yemen.name: Yemen
yemen.remarks: Socotra, off the Horn of Africa, has been isolated long enough that a third of its plants grow nowhere else. The marine life is similarly peculiar.

raja_ampat.name: Raja Ampat
raja_ampat.remarks: Fifteen hundred islands at the heart of the Coral Triangle, and the richest reef fish diversity ever recorded anywhere.

andaman_and_nicobar_islands.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
andaman_and_nicobar_islands.remarks: Five hundred islands, most closed to visitors, and some inhabited by people who have declined contact for tens of thousands of years.

ryukyu_islands.name: Ryukyu Islands
ryukyu_islands.remarks: Subtropical islands running south-west from Japan, with coral, hammerhead schools in winter, and a rock formation off Yonaguni that people continue to argue about.

similan_islands.name: Similan Islands
similan_islands.remarks: Granite boulders the size of houses, stacked underwater, with swim-throughs between them.
